audit.whatIsWrong: FABRICATED ABILITY NAME. Neeko's ultimate is called 'Tidal Break' in four separate places: content.whys[4], content.spikes[1].text, content.mid, and content.wants.foe[2]. There is no such ability. Neeko's R is Pop Blossom. 'Tidal Break' is Nautilus-adjacent flavour text that does not belong to any Neeko slot.
audit.why: Riot's kit for Neeko is Inherent Glamour (P), Blooming Burst (Q), Shapesplitter (W), Tangle-Barbs (E), Pop Blossom (R). Pop Blossom is also not a plain 'AOE stun': after a short preparation she leaps into the air knocking up all nearby enemies, then damages and stuns on landing — a knockup into a stun, and crucially the preparation is HIDDEN while she is disguised by Inherent Glamour. That last clause is the actual reason the level-6 read is dangerous and it was nowhere on the page.
audit.corrected: All four occurrences replaced with Pop Blossom, and the disguised wind-up added.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chart rows 0, 2 and 3 disagreed with the packet and with this page's own prose. Also the header read EVEN 6/10 for a 57.76% matchup that every other field describes as favoured.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is Swain, Swain, Skill, Swain, Skill, Swain, Swain and the mirror set rows 0/2/3 to Swain/Skill/Swain in both layers. The prose already said it: whys[0] gives Swain a level-1 kill threat on a champion with no dash, whys[2] says 'the edge disappears temporarily' at level 3, whys[3] and content.mid say 'Levels 4-5 are a grinding attrition window Swain almost always wins'. Rows 1, 4, 5 and 6 already matched and were left alone.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 2 and 3 flipped in both layers as one atomic group, with ratings rescaled; diff EVEN -> FAV with tone, diffRating, breakdown.difficulty and report[14] brought into line together so no new contradiction is created.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer never named a single real spike mechanic and the spikes array is out of chronological order — spikes[2].when is '1st item' while spikes[3].when is 'Lvl 4-5'.
audit.why: Swain's real spikes here are level 1 (E gives root threat against a champion with no dash), the Tangle-Barbs cooldown window at 4-5, and first item. The ordering issue is structural: the last card on the page reads as the latest spike and it is actually the earliest.
audit.corrected: tldr and the Do's now name the real spike mechanic and its cooldown. The spikes ordering is reported in notes rather than edited — reordering would mean swapping two entries' text AND when values and I would rather the user decide than shuffle cards silently.

audit.whatIsWrong: Tangle-Barbs' escalation was never stated: the page just calls it 'her root — extends through targets'.
audit.why: If the tangle kills an enemy or passes through a champion it becomes larger, faster, and roots for longer. That is why standing behind a low minion or a second champion is what actually gets you a long root, not the cast itself. 1000 range, 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d now states the range, the cooldown and the escalation.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid told the reader to 'bait the R by half-pressing R'. There is no half-press; Demonic Ascension is a single cast with Demonflare as a recast.
audit.why: Riot's text: Swain transforms and drains, and 'can cast Demonflare' as a second action. Nothing in the kit supports a partial or feinted first cast, so the instruction cannot be followed and reads as a mechanic the player is failing to find.
audit.corrected: Removed in the content.mid rewrite. The surrounding advice (bait, absorb fragments, recast Demonflare on her landing) is kept because it is sound and does not depend on the invented input.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a grinding attrition window Swain almost always wins — you have W-into-E layered poke, she has burst combos that require Tangle-Barbs to land. Treat Tangle-Barbs like Darius's Decimate: when it is on cooldown she has no reliable setup and dies to your pattern; when it is up, stand at maximum W range and do not commit. Watch for her W clone trick — she can swap with a clone to bait your E, so wait until the illusion fades or you confirm the real Neeko before throwing Nevermove. At level 6 be cautious: her R (Tidal Break) is an AOE stun that interrupts Demonic Ascension, so do not drain in a spot where she can walk up and unload it on you — bait the R by half-pressing R, absorb a few fragments, then recast Demonflare the instant she lands to punish the cast animation.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a grinding attrition window Swain almost always wins — you have W-into-E layered poke, she has burst combos that require Tangle-Barbs to land. Tangle-Barbs is 10-12s and grows larger and longer-rooting after it passes through a champion: when it is down she has no reliable setup and dies to your pattern; when it is up, stand at maximum W range and do not commit. Watch for her Shapesplitter clone — she can send it out to bait your E, so confirm the real Neeko before throwing Nevermove. At level 6 be cautious: Pop Blossom is a knockup into an AOE stun, and Inherent Glamour hides the preparation while she is disguised, so do not drain where she can walk up and unload — bait it, absorb a few fragments, then recast Demonflare the instant she lands.

notes: packet.suspectNames flags 'Use Vision of Empire' in wants.you[1] as a probable wrong name. It is a FALSE POSITIVE — Vision of Empire is the correct name for Swain's W and the string is right as written. The near-miss detector matched it against its own lowercase form at distance 4. Two things I did not edit and one is worth a look: (1) content.spikes is out of chronological order, spikes[2].when is '1st item' and spikes[3].when is 'Lvl 4-5', so the last card on the page is the earliest timing — fixing it means swapping both .text and .when across two entries and I would rather it be a deliberate change than a silent shuffle. (2) The 'interrupts Demonic Ascension' framing survives in content.wants.foe[2] in softened form ('knock you out of your drain'); Swain's R has no channel flag, so whether hard CC actually ends an active Ascension is unconfirmed from the kits — same open question I raised on swain__nautilus.
